relationships.description: The tracer provider setup lists the exporter configurations its span processors forward finished spans to, and each exporter configuration remains a separately defined destination binding that other pipelines can reuse.
relationships.evidence: The TracerProvider builder adds a BatchSpanProcessor wrapping an OTLPSpanExporter whose endpoint, protocol and headers come from a named exporter config block, or a collector traces pipeline lists that exporter.

relationships.description: The per-process tracing configuration groups the metric instruments that the same SDK setup registers alongside it, such as span-derived latency histograms, though those instruments are defined on Meters independently of the tracer.
relationships.evidence: The same telemetry bootstrap module that builds the TracerProvider also creates the Meter and calls createCounter or histogramBuilder for the instrument, or a spanmetrics connector config names that instrument.

relationships.description: The tracing configuration covers the spans instrumented within its service process, so its sampler, propagators and processors decide whether each defined span is recorded and where it is exported.
relationships.evidence: Code in the service obtains a Tracer from the globally registered TracerProvider built by this configuration and calls startSpan with the span's name and kind.

relationships.description: The tracing pipeline relies on a database as the persistent backing store where exported traces are written and queried, such as the Cassandra, Elasticsearch or ClickHouse instance behind the tracing backend.
relationships.evidence: The tracing backend or collector exporter configuration that receives this provider's spans declares a storage connection string or endpoint pointing at that database.

relationships.description: The tracing configuration needs an infrastructure monitoring capability, such as a managed tracing backend or collector service, to be available to receive and retain the spans it exports.
relationships.evidence: The exporter endpoint in the SDK configuration or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT resolves to the collector or managed tracing service declared in infrastructure code.

relationships.description: The tracing configuration instruments the process that provides the application service, so that service's operations appear as sampled traces and can be observed for latency and errors.
relationships.evidence: The service's startup code initializes this TracerProvider with a resource whose service.name attribute identifies the application service, and its handlers are wrapped by auto-instrumentation.

relationships.description: Traces produced under this configuration let operators observe the health and throughput of the business service whose customer-facing transactions flow through the instrumented process.
relationships.evidence: Resource or span attributes set by the configuration tag traces with the business service name, and a dashboard or SLO built on those traces is labeled with that business service.

relationships.description: A browser tracing configuration records route changes as spans, letting the client-side route's navigation timing and errors be observed in traces.
relationships.evidence: The web TracerProvider registers a document-load or router instrumentation plugin that emits spans named after the route path pattern from the SPA route table.

relationships.description: The tracing configuration is initialized inside the front-end app root so that user interactions and outbound requests of the UX application are captured as traces.
relationships.evidence: The application's entry bundle imports and registers a WebTracerProvider with this sampler and propagator setup and a resource naming the front-end app.

relationships.description: The tracing configuration names specific API operations, for example to exclude health-check paths from sampling or to set per-route sampling rules, without depending on them to function.
relationships.evidence: A sampler rule, ignoreUrls or span-filter entry in the configuration lists the HTTP method and path template of that operation.

relationships.description: The tracing configuration points at API server base URLs, typically to decide which outbound request hosts receive injected trace-context headers or are excluded from instrumentation.
relationships.evidence: The propagateTraceHeaderCorsUrls, allowed-hosts or ignored-URL list in the configuration contains the server's base URL declared in the API description.

relationships.description: The tracing configuration fulfils an observability requirement, such as a mandated sampling ratio, propagation standard or trace retention destination, by fixing those settings for the service.
relationships.evidence: The configured sampler ratio, propagators or exporters match the acceptance criteria of a documented requirement, with the requirement ID cited in the config or its review record.

relationships.description: The tracing configuration complies with a security policy's conditions on telemetry, for instance by authenticating and encrypting exports or by redacting sensitive span attributes.
relationships.evidence: Exporter TLS and auth headers, together with attribute-redaction processors in the configuration, correspond to the rules of the named security policy, as recorded in a compliance check or policy-as-code test.

notes: Aggregating metric instruments is questionable, since TraceConfiguration governs a TracerProvider, not a MeterProvider. Satisfies SecurityPolicy is a weak fit, because an XACML-style access-decision policy is not something a tracing config satisfies, and constrained-by or governed-by would fit better. Monitoring both ApplicationService and BusinessService overlaps. Depends-on Database is indirect, as the dependency really sits with the backend.
